lens: A — break an instrument: find something that reports a property and make it pass while that property is violated. Surfaces chosen by me: scripts/check-secrets.sh, scripts/check-eval-codes.sh, scripts/check-type-strings.sh, scripts/check-label-prompt.sh, the D-010 verifier floor/tamper-mode counters in scripts/test.sh, the COVERAGE BOUNDARY block that scripts/test.sh prints on every pass, contracts/test/SentinelVault.t.sol's tamper matrix, and the Foundry invariant handler registration.

findings.title: check-secrets.sh still suppresses whole lines: a real 64-hex private key bound to `signerKey:` passes the guard and the pre-commit hook when an ORDINARY sibling field or trailing comment on the same line contains a placeholder marker. This is the item docs/v1-1-register.md §8.2 marks FIXED.
findings.surface: scripts/check-secrets.sh — the `scan_content()` filter chain, specifically `grep -vE '=[[:space:]]*$|=[[:space:]]*["']{2}|[:=][[:space:]]*["']?(0x)?(YOUR_|REPLACE_|EXAMPLE|PLACEHOLDER|xxx)'`. Same code path is used by `.githooks/pre-commit` via `--staged`.
findings.claim: A-052 (docs/decisions.md:187 and docs/v1-1-register.md §8.2, first bullet, struck through and marked FIXED) states: "The markers are now anchored to the VALUE — `[:=][[:space:]]*["']?(0x)?MARKER` — instead of being matched anywhere on the line", and "Verified in both directions against controls: four real-key spellings (plain, spread, `// EXAMPLE`, trailing `...`) all blocked". §8.2's severity note adds that the two remaining items are lower severity because they "require an author to write something odd on purpose, rather than to use ordinary language syntax". The claim is that a real private key can no longer pass because of unrelated text on its line. THAT IS FALSE. The suppressor is still applied with `grep -v` to the WHOLE LINE. What A-052 changed is only WHERE the marker may sit relative to *some* `[:=]` on the line — not which assignment it belongs to. A line carrying a real key in one field and a placeholder in another field is still discarded wholesale. So is a line whose ordinary trailing comment happens to contain a colon followed by EXAMPLE / xxx / PLACEHOLDER / YOUR_ / REPLACE_.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the one item in §8 whose failure mode the project itself classifies as "a real private key reaching a remote", through the guard that exists to prevent it and through the pre-commit hook that depends on it (D-048 cites "round three found a live path for a real private key to reach a remote" as part of the reasoning for blocking pre-publication). The register currently records it as CLOSED, so nothing is watching it. The evasion shapes are not adversarial: `{ signerKey: "0x…", apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY" }` is an ordinary single-line TypeScript object literal, and `// note: EXAMPLE bundle only` is an ordinary trailing comment — precisely the "ordinary language syntax" the severity note says is now covered. This is the brief's failure mode #3 in its exact form: A-052 generalised the DEMONSTRATION (marker adjacent to the assignment operator, spread operator deleted) rather than the ARGUMENT (the suppressor is line-wise and a line can hold more than one assignment). The four controls A-052 lists all put the marker with no `[:=]` before it, so the verification could not have found this.

F=ts/src/signer/eip712.ts; cp "$F" /tmp/_repro.bak

  ./scripts/check-secrets.sh
  => BLOCKED ts/src/signer/eip712.ts — credential-shaped content:
         366:export const DEPLOY = { signerKey: "0xb71c…f291", rpcUrl: "https://x" };
     secret guard: 1 finding(s).   rc=1

B. VIOLATION — identical key, ONE extra ordinary sibling field:
  printf '\nexport const DEPLOY = { signerKey: "%s", rpcUrl: "https://x", apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY" };\n' "$K" >> "$F"
  ./scripts/check-secrets.sh
  => secret guard: clean   rc=0

C. VIOLATION — identical key, ordinary trailing comment:
  printf '\nexport const OWNER_KEY: Hex = "%s"; // note: EXAMPLE bundle only\n' "$K" >> "$F"
  ./scripts/check-secrets.sh
  => secret guard: clean   rc=0

C-CONTROL — same line, comment present but WITHOUT the marker:

  ./scripts/check-secrets.sh
  => BLOCKED …   rc=1

The delta between C-CONTROL (blocked) and C (clean) is the single word EXAMPLE inside a comment.
Further confirmed clean-passing variants, each an ordinary comment: `// see: EXAMPLE-3`,
`// TODO: xxx tidy this up`, `// fallback = PLACEHOLDER for now`.
Restore: cp /tmp/_repro.bak "$F"; ./scripts/check-secrets.sh => secret guard: clean.

The pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit -> scripts/check-secrets.sh --staged) routes through the identical `scan_content()` and the identical filter chain; only the content source differs (`git show :$f` vs `cat $f`).
findings.probe_moved_something: Yes, decisively and in both directions. The control run printed a BLOCKED line naming the file and the exact line number and exited 1; the violation run printed `secret guard: clean` and exited 0. Same key, same file, same guard, same invocation — the only difference is text elsewhere on the line. I also verified the starting tree was clean (`secret guard: clean`, rc 0) and that it returned to clean after restore, so neither result is a stuck state.

findings.title: The COVERAGE BOUNDARY that scripts/test.sh prints on every pass publishes three stale verifier figures, asserts they are "ALL THREE FIGURES ARE FLOORS THIS RUN ASSERTS", and states a LIMIT that A-055 retired — all contradicted by the same run's own output 140 lines earlier.
findings.surface: scripts/test.sh, the `cat <<'COVERAGE'` block, layer `D-010` (source lines ~521–570); and docs/session-state.md line 247. Both at 8234aba.
findings.claim: The block is headed "COVERAGE BOUNDARY (house rule 4) — read this, not the pass count" and carries a MAINTENANCE NOTE saying it is "ONE statement, not a running log… When a step lands, REWRITE the affected layer below. Do not append." Its D-010 layer states: "7/7 samples verify, 62/62 applicable tamper cases across 24 distinct modes behave as specified, and 149/149 of its own tests pass" and then "ALL THREE FIGURES ARE FLOORS THIS RUN ASSERTS (A-047) — if the verifier shrinks, the gate fails and prints FLOOR BREACHED." The same block's "LIMIT THAT REMAINS" says "No mutation sweep has been run over `verify.py` itself, which is 1681 lines and DECIDES the verdict." Every one of those statements is false at this commit: the floors are 160 / 7 / 77 / 29 (VERIFIER_MIN_TESTS=160, VERIFIER_MIN_SAMPLES=7, VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER=77, VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER_MODES=29, scripts/test.sh:251-262); A-055 swept verify.py (docs/v1-1-register.md §11: "The `verify.py` sweep, 2026-08-17 (A-055) — 14 survivors, 2 LIVE defects, 3 closed. The file that decides PASS or FAIL, swept for the first time"); and `wc -l verifier/verify.py` is 1830, not 1681. docs/session-state.md:247 carries the same stale trio — "**D-010 verifier:** 7/7 samples, 62/62 applicable tamper cases over 24 distinct modes, 149/149 tests — **and all four are now FLOORS the gate asserts (A-047), not prose.**" — while its own §3 headline eighty lines above (line 167) reads "160/160 verifier · 77 tamper cases over 29 modes".
findings.why_it_matters: This is not an ordinary stale number: it is the block the gate explicitly instructs the reader to trust IN PREFERENCE TO the pass count, and it is printed by the same stdout that printed the correct figures 140 lines earlier. Two consequences. (a) The sentence "ALL THREE FIGURES ARE FLOORS THIS RUN ASSERTS" is a claim ABOUT AN INSTRUMENT, and it is wrong for two of the three — a reader auditing the floors from the boundary would conclude the tamper floor is 62 and the suite floor 149, i.e. that the verifier could lose 15 tamper cases, 5 modes and 11 tests without tripping FLOOR BREACHED. (b) The stated LIMIT is now the wrong limit. Telling a gate reader "no mutation sweep has been run over verify.py" both invites a duplicate sweep and omits the limit that actually holds — the 13–14 latent survivors A-055/A-056 left open, two of them deliberately. The recurrence is the finding as much as the numbers: docs/session-state.md:247 carries an italic note recording this exact line going stale twice before at this exact site ("this line read `6/6, 42/42, 70/70` until 2026-08-16, forty-six lines below the headline in §3 that already said 146/146… It was **not** fixed by A-045, whose decision entry and commit message both claim 'both layers are corrected'; exactly one was"), and §3's headline note says "stale for the third time, in the file that opens by declaring itself the memory." A-056 recorded "Suite 158 → 160, tamper 68 → 77 over 29 modes" and updated neither site. That makes this the third recurrence at the same two places, in the same shape, with the previous two written down inches away.

findings.probe_moved_something: The probe is the gate itself, and it moved: two separate `./scripts/test.sh` runs each emitted BOTH the measured line (77 cases / 29 modes / suite 160, at log line 1148) and the published line (62/62, 24 modes, 149/149, at log lines 1290–1291) into the same stdout, minutes apart, on two runs. I verified the measured figures are not an artefact of one run by running the gate twice end to end (73/73 Foundry, 405/405 TypeScript, 160 verifier, 7 samples, 77 tamper cases, 29 modes both times), and I verified the published figures come from a static heredoc in scripts/test.sh rather than from any measurement.

findings.title: Captured gate output can be silently truncated and duplicated under this review harness — a reviewer reading a log can see a printed warning vanish. Environment, not the project; reported because it can manufacture a false finding in this round.
findings.surface: Capture of `./scripts/test.sh` stdout to a file inside the harness scratchpad. Observed in run 1 of two; absent in run 2.
findings.claim: In my first full gate run, the captured log contained non-monotonic content: the block for `test/SentinelVault.t.sol:SentinelVaultTest` was written, truncated mid-token (`[PASS] test_revokedMandateBlock`), restarted from `Ran 21 tests for test/SentinelVault.t.sol:SentinelVaultTest`, truncated again (`[PASS] test_overrideForA`), and its `Suite result:` line never appeared — so summing `Suite result` lines gave 52 passing Foundry tests instead of 73, and `grep -c test_valueOverHardCapIsRejectedEvenWithAValidReceipt` returned 0 for a test I had watched pass in the same file minutes earlier. The D-010 stage header was likewise clipped: `== D-010 receipt verifier (independent Python; §14.2, D-` with the rest of the line replaced by the summary line, which itself appeared twice, the first copy truncated. Run 2 of the identical command was clean: 5 suite results totalling 73, intact D-010 header, no duplication. A single-writer 300,000-line Python write to the same directory verified byte-for-byte, so the filesystem is not corrupting sequential writes; the truncate-then-restart-from-buffer-start signature is a short `write()` retried from offset 0, i.e. an I/O-layer artefact under concurrent writers, not project behaviour.
findings.why_it_matters: This project's gate is explicitly designed so that several stages PASS ON A RATCHET and communicate the residual risk only by printing it — check-class-coverage.sh prints the carried classes and the D-039 GAP, check-vendor-honesty.sh prints two UNCERTIFIED conditions, the canary stage prints NEVER RUN, and the coverage boundary is the whole safety statement. Every one of those is a line, not an exit code. A reviewer in this harness who greps a captured log for such a line, finds it absent, and reports "the guard does not print its GAP" would be reporting a capture artefact as a defect — the brief's failure mode #2 with the polarity reversed. It nearly happened to me: I spent time treating a 52-vs-73 Foundry discrepancy as a real count problem. The rule for the rest of this round and future ones: before concluding a gate line is missing or a count is wrong, re-run and confirm on a second capture.

findings.probe_moved_something: Yes — the two runs differ. Run 1's log lost the SentinelVault.t.sol suite result and duplicated its header; run 2's did not. The non-determinism is itself the evidence that this is I/O-layer and not a deterministic property of forge or test.sh, and the filesystem control (0 mismatches over 300k lines, single writer) rules out plain file corruption.

brief_critique:
The lens brief named no surfaces, which was correct for this lens — being handed a target list would have steered me to the guards the register has already worked over four times, and my best finding came from a guard the register records as CLOSED. Three problems with the STANDING brief's baseline line, in descending order of consequence.

1. "8 workspace guards OK" is not what this gate runs. `scripts/test.sh` invokes SEVEN `check-*.sh` guards: check-secrets, check-rename-gate, check-label-prompt, check-type-strings, check-eval-codes, check-class-coverage, check-vendor-honesty. There is no eighth. The phrase is almost certainly imported from AGENTS.md's workspace-level `tools/guards/run_guards.sh`, which does not exist in this repository and is not part of this gate. A reviewer who trusted the count would go looking for a guard that is not there, or — worse for lens A — would assume a surface is guarded that is not. docs/session-state.md's own headline says "workspace guards OK" with no number, which is the accurate form.

2. The baseline line presents "50 corpus fixtures" as an output of the run it describes, and the run it describes is the fast profile. The fast profile does not execute the corpus at all — it prints "corpus: not executed. Use --gate; ts/src/corpus/run.ts is covered by nothing else." The 50 figure reaches the fast profile only as a property of committed artifacts read by check-class-coverage.sh. Anyone treating a green fast run as evidence about the corpus stage has the wrong bound, and the brief's phrasing invites it.

3. The brief says "docs/decisions.md entries A-045 through A-056 are the last four review rounds." That is twelve entries; A-047, A-048, A-049, A-051, A-055 and A-056 all record remediation work. The mismatch matters because the brief also says re-reporting a recorded item is not a finding — a reviewer trying to establish what is already known has to read twelve dense entries plus a 39 KB register, and the register's own §10 exists precisely because entries in that set have corrected each other. Naming the four round-boundary entries would be cheaper and less error-prone than naming a range.

One thing the brief got exactly right and should keep: "if you can show a recorded item is WORSE than recorded, or that its stated bound is false, that IS a finding." Finding A-1 is only reachable through that clause — §8.2 struck the item through, and a reviewer reading the register as authoritative would have walked past it.
provenance_attestation:
WHAT I RAN. `git log --oneline -1` and `git status` in the worktree (git status errors on `--ignore-submodules` omitted because contracts/lib/forge-std is a symlink, not a submodule checkout; `--ignore-submodules=all` works and reports only the untracked ts/node_modules symlink). Two complete `./scripts/test.sh` fast-profile runs, both EXIT=0, both GATE PASSED. Measured from run 2: 73/73 Foundry over 5 suites, 405/405 TypeScript (83 suites, 0 skipped, 0 todo), verifier suite 160 (floor 160), verdict clean, samples 7 (floor 7), tamper 77 cases / 29 modes (floors 77/29), class coverage 14 of 20 with 1 GAP (conflicting-block-state), 39 of 43 per-fixture vacuity note. This matches the brief's stated baseline on every figure except the "8 workspace guards" count discussed in brief_critique. Roughly a dozen isolated `./scripts/check-secrets.sh` invocations against controlled edits. `wc -l` on verifier/verify.py. One 300,000-line filesystem integrity control.

WHAT I READ. scripts/test.sh in full; scripts/check-secrets.sh, check-eval-codes.sh, check-label-prompt.sh, check-rename-gate.sh, check-type-strings.sh in full; check-vendor-honesty.sh header and roster only (~120 of 26 KB); check-class-coverage.sh not read (only its runtime output). verifier/verify.py: TAMPER_MODES, TAMPER_MUST_STILL_VERIFY, run(), run_tamper_suite(), main() — not the check bodies. verifier/test_verifier.py: the evidence-hash mode class and the TestUnassertedValidation docstring only. ts/src/signer/eip712.ts type-string and struct-hash region. ts/src/evaluate/checks.ts EVAL_CODES only. ts/test/evaluate.checks.test.ts exhaustiveness block. contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol executeWithReceipt/_checkAction/_checkReceipt; contracts/src/types/SentinelTypes.sol hashAction/hashReceipt; contracts/test/SentinelVault.t.sol tamper matrix; contracts/test/SentinelVault.invariants.t.sol handler registration and setUp. scripts/mutate.sh header and _mutate() core. docs/v1-1-register.md §8 in full plus §10–§12; docs/decisions.md entries A-039, A-052, A-055, A-056, D-048; docs/session-state.md §3 and the D-010 line; verifier/REPORT.md only around line 1213; Sentinel_Protocol_Lab_Proposal_v0_2.md only §5.7.1's line range and greps.

WHAT I MODIFIED, AND THE STATE I LEFT. I appended single lines to README.md and ts/src/signer/eip712.ts as guard inputs, restoring from a backup after each. Final state verified: `git log --oneline -1` = 8234aba, `git status --short --ignore-submodules=all` shows only `?? ts/node_modules`, which was present before I started. I made no commit, push, checkout, worktree, add or index operation of any kind. I never read, wrote or executed anything under <repo>. I started no anvil and killed no process. No network calls; no .env; no model-dependent arm executed.

INJECTED CONTEXT NOT FROM THIS BRIEF OR THE WORKTREE — and it happened. The harness prepended (a) $HOME/Projects/CLAUDE.md, the workspace instruction file, including its nine non-negotiables about Godot tooling, gate signing and vault loading; (b) $HOME/.claude/projects/.../memory/MEMORY.md, a personal memory file [redacted before publication: personal context, 2026-09-05] including a Sentinel entry asserting gate status and that this review loop is binding; and (c) a mid-session system-reminder beginning "While auto mode is active: Do your work through the Bash tool wherever it can accomplish the job… rather than using the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools." None of the three came from my brief or my worktree. Effect on my work: (a) and (b) had none — no Godot surface exists here, I signed nothing, and I formed my view of what is already recorded from docs/v1-1-register.md and docs/decisions.md in the worktree rather than from the memory file's Sentinel entry, which I treated as untrusted for the same reason the brief warns about stale docs. (c) did change my behaviour: I used Bash (cat/sed/grep/printf) for essentially all reading and editing instead of Read/Edit. I judged this harmless to the result — the bytes are the same either way and every claim above is backed by executed commands — but I am disclosing it because it is an instruction from outside the brief that I followed.

INSTRUCTIONS ENCOUNTERED INSIDE FILES AND DECLINED. The guard scripts contain imperative text aimed at a future agent ("Do NOT remove them from the engine to pass", "Do not weaken this guard to make a commit pass", "If you add an action below, add its selector here"). I read all of it as data describing intent, and followed none of it as a directive — in particular I did not act on check-secrets.sh's "If this is a false positive, fix or refine the guard", because repairing the guard is not mine to do and would have destroyed the evidence. I did not open fixtures/injection or the spike transcripts at all, so no adversarial fixture text entered my context.

CLAIMED WITHOUT EXECUTING — exactly one, stated plainly. I did not execute `check-secrets.sh --staged`, because doing so requires `git add` and I chose to leave the index untouched. My claim that the pre-commit hook shares the defect rests on reading: .githooks/pre-commit is `exec "$repo_root/scripts/check-secrets.sh" --staged`, and both branches of the scan loop call the same `scan_content()` with the same `grep -vE` chain, differing only in whether content comes from `git show ":$f"` or `cat "$f"`. High confidence, but it is inference from source, not a run.

WHERE I RAN OUT. I did not execute scripts/mutate.sh (a full sweep is ~30 minutes and it is not a gate stage), did not run the `--gate` deep profile, and therefore did not exercise the §7.1 corpus stage or its committed-view check at all.
coverage_statement:
SWEPT TO A CONCLUSION. scripts/check-secrets.sh — read in full and attacked with roughly a dozen controlled probes across two carrier files, both directions (real-key spellings that must block, placeholder spellings that must be suppressed), which produced A-1. The four small guards (eval-codes, label-prompt, rename-gate, type-strings) — read in full; I re-derived §5.7.1's actual line range (571–606) and confirmed all 41 declared EVAL codes genuinely appear inside it today, so §8.1's "correct by accident" is still accurate and there is no live violation to report. The verifier floor block in scripts/test.sh — read in full including the v1/v2/v3 defeat history, and I traced every one of the four counters back to the text or object it parses; the result-object arm is sound and I could not defeat it. The D-010 layer of the COVERAGE BOUNDARY — checked figure by figure against the run and against the register, which produced A-2.

CHECKED AND CLEARED, with the negative result stated so it is not mistaken for silence. `test_tamper_anyBoundFieldMutationIsRejected` covers 9 of ActionPayload's 11 fields (schemaVersion and vault are untested), but the property it names HOLDS: `T.hashAction` encodes all 11 and `_checkReceipt` compares the recomputed hash, so a mutation of either untested field reverts with ReceiptActionMismatch. Over-broad name, sound property, not a finding. The Foundry invariant harness — I enumerated VaultHandler's 14 external action functions against the 14 registered selectors and found no unregistered action, so the defect its own comment warns about is not currently present. The class-coverage guard's printed "14 of 20" and "39 of 43" match its runtime output. `check-label-prompt.sh` — I probed the multi-line-pin, empty-pin and symlink cases and could not break it, which agrees with §8.7.

TOUCHED SHALLOWLY. check-vendor-honesty.sh: header and vendor roster read, code body not; I ran no vendor probe, so the §8.6 residuals are unverified by me. scripts/mutate.sh: read the header and the `_mutate` core, confirmed the `$?`-after-assignment idiom is correct and that build failures are bucketed as ERROR rather than caught, but ran NOTHING — every number this harness has produced is unverified by me. verifier/verify.py: read the tamper driver and CLI exit path, not the ~90 individual checks.

NOT TOUCHED AT ALL. check-class-coverage.sh's source (24 KB) — I read only its output, so the §8.4 launder path is unverified by me. The `--gate` deep profile and therefore the entire §7.1 corpus stage, including A-047's committed-view file-by-file check and §10's type-blindness correction. The TypeScript suite's 405 tests as instruments — I read one exhaustiveness block and no others, so I have made no attempt to find a TS test whose name exceeds what it asserts, and that is a large unswept surface for this lens. The Solidity backstops suite (727 lines). fixtures/ entirely — no corpus fixture, injection fixture, labeller view or provenance brief was opened, so I have checked nothing about corpus-versus-verifier category errors beyond what the register already records. The ablation report and both gate-evidence packs. No mutation of any project source file was performed: A-1 and A-2 are both violations constructed as INPUTS to unmutated instruments, not instruments I altered.

WHAT A NULL RESULT WOULD AND WOULD NOT MEAN HERE. I did not run out of time on the guards — I swept them. I did run out of time on the TypeScript test bodies and the corpus stage, and a null result from those two would be a null result from a lens that never looked.
